## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammahetukathā* (Kv 8.11) is a debate located in the eighth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. The controversy examines the proposition that an arahant can fall away from arahantship on account of past actions (*kammahetu arahā arahattā parihāyati*) [Dutt 1945; Hazra 1994]. According to the commentary and doxographical traditions, this thesis was maintained by the Pubbaseliya and Sammitīya schools [Dutt 1945]. Opponents argued that if a person had slandered an arahant in a prior life (*purimabhava*), the karmic consequence of that past slander could cause them to retrogress from arahantship [Dutt 1945; Bareau 1955]. The orthodox Theravāda position rejects this claim, insisting that an arahant does not lose the state of liberation due to past deeds [Bareau 1955].

**Sources**

- [Dutt 1945] Nalinaksha Dutt, Early Monastic Buddhism, vol. 2 (1945) — identifies the thesis and its attribution to the Pubbaseliyas and Sammitīyas concerning past slander
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — places the thesis within chapter 8 of the Kathāvatthu
- [Bareau 1955] André Bareau, Les sectes bouddhiques du Petit Véhicule (1955) — details the sectarian arguments regarding fall from arahantship due to past deeds and the Theravādin denial
